advancements.royaumedesidees.allegorie_v: Leave Plato's Cave and finally see the light (and be dazzled by it).
advancements.royaumedesidees.racine.desc: Take up, read, and step through the bookshelf portal.
block.royaumedesidees.confessionnal.aide: In the Kingdom, type /confesse followed by your sin within 5 blocks: one level of Guilt less.
block.royaumedesidees.etal_verger.aide: Right-click with an emerald: 3 pears, honestly bought.
block.royaumedesidees.feuilles_poirier.a: Right-click leaves laden with pears: pick a pear (that is theft).
block.royaumedesidees.pupitre_ambroise.a: 8-block zone of silence: the chat is muted there, monsters cannot see players.
commande.royaumedesidees.structures.a_re: will be placed again when a player comes near
commande.royaumedesidees.structures.sans: The Kingdom dimension is not loaded.
item.royaumedesidees.lanterne_diogene.ci: "I am looking for a man." (Diogenes of Sinope)
item.royaumedesidees.lanterne_diogene.ef: When held: reveals Shadows within 8 blocks.
item.royaumedesidees.livre_confessions.c: "You have made us for yourself, and our heart is restless until it rests in you." Right-click: heals nearby players.
item.royaumedesidees.poire.citation: Honestly bought. Not as good as the other kind: Augustine noticed it too.
item.royaumedesidees.poire_volee.citatio: "It was not the pear I loved, but the theft." (after the Confessions, II)
item.royaumedesidees.sceau_conversion.ci: First of the four Seals. The Altar of the City of God awaits it.
item.royaumedesidees.tolle_lege.citation: "Take up and read; take up and read." (Confessions, VIII)
item.royaumedesidees.tolle_lege.effet: Right-click a 4 by 5 frame of bookshelves (empty in the middle), with a lantern against each corner: opens the portal to the Kingdom.
livre.royaumedesidees.comptes.page1:
Election of Rouen
Taille of 1641

   3 livres 7 sols 4 deniers
+ 12 livres 15 sols 9 deniers
+  2 livres 19 sols 11 deniers
= ?

20 sols make a livre,
12 deniers make a sol.
livre.royaumedesidees.comptes.page2:
My father spends his nights on these.

One would need a machine to do such sums.

B. P., aged 19
livre.royaumedesidees.hexaemeron.page1:
Hexaemeron

The six days of Creation, preached by Ambrose in Milan.

Augustine came to hear him, first for his fine words, then for what he said.
livre.royaumedesidees.hexaemeron.page2:
"When he read, his eyes ran over the pages and his heart sought out the meaning, but his voice and tongue were at rest."

(Confessions, VI, 3)
livre.royaumedesidees.platoniciens.page1:
Books of the Platonists

Translated from Greek into Latin by Marius Victorinus.

Augustine read them in Milan, in 386, in this very house.
livre.royaumedesidees.platoniciens.page2:
He found in them that in the beginning was the Word, and the Word was God.

He did not find that the Word was made flesh.

(Confessions, VII, 9)
livre.royaumedesidees.platoniciens.page3:
Remember the Cave: what you took for the world was only its shadow.

Plato shows the light; he does not tell the way.
livre.royaumedesidees.romains.page1:
Epistle to the Romans, XIII, 13-14

Let us walk honestly, as in the day; not in rioting and drunkenness, not in chambering and wantonness,
livre.royaumedesidees.romains.page2: not in strife and envying. But put ye on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh, to fulfil the lusts thereof.
livre.royaumedesidees.romains.page3:
Augustine read this passage in silence, here, on this bench.

"As if a light of peace had been poured into my heart, all the darkness of doubt fled away."

(Confessions, VIII, 12)
message.royaumedesidees.astuce.culpabili: You have Guilt (the icon at the top right): it slows you down and gets worse with each sin. To be freed, type /confesse followed by your sin near a Confessional (there is one in the centre of the island, around 18, -14).
message.royaumedesidees.astuce.grace: You gain Grace (the golden gauge at the bottom right): by confessing, feeding Monica, taking Adeodatus's challenges, being hit without striking back, and with quests. It is used to change your Way, and later at the Altar.
message.royaumedesidees.astuce.royaume: Welcome to the Kingdom of Ideas. Type /quete at any time: you will see your quests, what to do and where to go. Right-click characters to talk to them.
message.royaumedesidees.astuce.silence: Silentium: here Ambrose reads. The chat is muted, and monsters cannot see you.
message.royaumedesidees.bapteme.annonce: Ambrose baptises %1$s, as he did Augustine at Easter 387. The Kingdom has one more convert.
message.royaumedesidees.caverne.enchaine: You are chained facing the wall, like Plato's prisoners. Break your chains.
message.royaumedesidees.caverne.lanterne: By the path, an old lantern was waiting for you. "I am looking for a man," said Diogenes.
message.royaumedesidees.caverne.lumiere: Your eyes, used to the shadows, burn in the daylight.
message.royaumedesidees.caverne.tenebres: Back in the Cave, your sun-filled eyes see nothing but darkness.
message.royaumedesidees.confession.alleg: Your conscience feels lighter. Guilt left: %1$s.
message.royaumedesidees.confession.hors_: Here your conscience is silent: Guilt and confession only exist in the Kingdom.
message.royaumedesidees.confession.loin: You need a Confessional to confess. There is one near the Altar, in the centre of the island.
message.royaumedesidees.confession.repet: *Slap!* You already confessed that. Augustine wrote thirteen books without repeating himself once: find another sin, or go and think it over.
message.royaumedesidees.confession.rien: Augustine wrote thirteen books of them; you really have nothing?
message.royaumedesidees.confession.trop_: Your confession is too long (%1$s characters at most). Augustine needed thirteen books.
Easy: wait %1$s more seconds before your next confession.
message.royaumedesidees.confessionnal.mo: To confess, type /confesse followed by your sin.
message.royaumedesidees.etal.achat: You honestly buy %1$s pears. They look less tasty.
message.royaumedesidees.etal.ecriteau: "One emerald in the box, %1$s pears for you. Or else, you steal them in the orchards…"
message.royaumedesidees.figuier.voix: A child's voice from the house next door: "Take up and read; take up and read."
message.royaumedesidees.grace.don: Grace is a gift, not a wage.
message.royaumedesidees.grace.rien: No Grace this time (%1$s). It cannot be earned.
message.royaumedesidees.impots.raison: You now follow the Way of Reason: you mine faster in the Kingdom, but Grace comes to you half as much.
message.royaumedesidees.journal.autres: Also: Adeodatus (villa tablinum, around -200, -197) sets maths challenges; Monica can be fed with a right-click holding food; changing your Way costs 50 Grace, with Pascal or Ambrose.
message.royaumedesidees.journal.conversi: Augustine, in the orchard lane (around -322, -169), has something for you to do. Talk to him.
4/4. Go and find Ambrose at the library (around -180, -330), and talk to him.
3/4. Weep under the garden fig tree (around -260, -260): crouch (Shift) for 5 seconds under its branches.
1/4. Steal 3 pears (right-click laden leaves) with Augustine nearby, in the orchards (around -330, -170).
3/4. Read the Epistle to the Romans on the lectern of Alypius's bench, in the fig tree garden (right-click).
2/4. Stay 60 seconds near Ambrose's lectern, at the library (around -180, -330), without writing in the chat.
message.royaumedesidees.journal.impots.a: Pascal, in his cell on the Port-Royal mound (around 300, -290), needs help with his father's accounts. Talk to him.
message.royaumedesidees.journal.impots.e: Talk to Pascal (around 300, -290) and give him his sums in the chat.
message.royaumedesidees.journal.impots.f: Done: the accounts of Rouen are right.
message.royaumedesidees.livre_confession: You read a page of the Confessions: %1$s soul(s) soothed.
This book speaks only to converted hearts.
Outside the Kingdom, the book is silent.
message.royaumedesidees.monique.arrive: §dSaint Monica§r hurries to you, in tears: you are the greatest sinner in the Kingdom. She will follow you until you are converted. (She accepts food: right-click holding something to eat.)
message.royaumedesidees.monique.consolee: §dMonica§r weeps with joy: "The son of so many tears cannot perish." She goes back to the garden, at peace.
message.royaumedesidees.monique.quitte: §dMonica§r leaves you for %1$s, who needs her more than you.
message.royaumedesidees.monique.rentre: §dMonica§r dries her tears and goes back to pray in the villa garden.
message.royaumedesidees.monique.revient: §dMonica§r comes back to pray for you: no one here has a heavier soul.
message.royaumedesidees.ombre.intouchabl: It is only a shadow: your blow goes straight through.
message.royaumedesidees.ombre.statue: It was only a wooden statue. Diogenes is still looking for a man.
message.royaumedesidees.portail.allume: "Take up and read; take up and read." The portal opens.
message.royaumedesidees.portail.dans_roy: No more reading here: look for the way out.
message.royaumedesidees.portail.incomple: The book stays silent: you need a 4 by 5 bookshelf frame, empty inside, with a lantern against each corner.
message.royaumedesidees.quete.bapteme: "As if a light of peace had been poured into my heart…" Quest 4/4: "The baptism". Go and find Ambrose at the library, and talk to him.
message.royaumedesidees.quete.figuier: Ambrose finally looks up and points to the fig tree garden. Quest 3/4: "Take up and read". Weep under the fig tree (around -260, -260): crouch (Shift) for 5 seconds under its branches.
message.royaumedesidees.quete.figuier_in: You weep under the fig tree, without knowing why. Augustine, in the orchards, could tell you.
message.royaumedesidees.quete.figuier_tr: You weep under the fig tree, but your hour has not come yet. (/quete)
message.royaumedesidees.quete.larmes: You weep under the fig tree… (%1$s / %2$s)
message.royaumedesidees.quete.poires: Conversion quest, 1/4: "The pears of Thagaste". Steal 3 pears (right-click laden leaves) with Augustine nearby. (/quete to see where you are.)
message.royaumedesidees.quete.romains: Go back to Alypius's bench (the half-circle marble bench in the garden), where you left the Apostle's book, and read it (right-click the lectern).
message.royaumedesidees.quete.silence: Conversion quest, 2/4: "Ambrose's silence". Go to the library (around -180, -330) and stay 60 seconds near Ambrose's lectern, without writing anything.
message.royaumedesidees.quete.silence_ro: You tried to speak: the silence starts over.
pnj.royaumedesidees.adeodat.attends: I'm waiting for your answer. In the chat.
pnj.royaumedesidees.adeodat.bonjour: Hello. My father says I was born of his sin. I prefer mathematics.
pnj.royaumedesidees.adeodat.coup: *sighs* Hitting a genius does not make you smarter. I checked.
pnj.royaumedesidees.adeodat.defi: What is %1$s? You have %2$s seconds. Answer in the chat.
pnj.royaumedesidees.adeodat.rate: It was %1$s. I had it before you finished reading the question.
pnj.royaumedesidees.adeodat.repos: One challenge at a time. Come back in %1$s seconds, even geniuses breathe.
pnj.royaumedesidees.ambroise.bapteme: *Ambrose puts down his book, pours water on your head, and finally speaks.* I baptise you.
pnj.royaumedesidees.ambroise.bonjour: *Ambrose looks up from his book, then down again, without a word.*
pnj.royaumedesidees.ambroise.coup: *Ambrose turns a page, without a word.*
pnj.royaumedesidees.ambroise.pas_assez_d: *Ambrose shakes his head: changing your Way costs %1$s Grace.*
pnj.royaumedesidees.ambroise.retour_coeu: *Ambrose smiles and traces a cross on your forehead.* You return to the Way of the Heart.
pnj.royaumedesidees.ambroise.silence: *Ambrose puts a finger to his lips, and goes on reading.*
pnj.royaumedesidees.augustin_jeune.bonjo: Hey! You look far too well-behaved. There's a cure for that: pears, over there.
pnj.royaumedesidees.augustin_jeune.coup: *bursts out laughing* You hit the way you steal: half-heartedly!
pnj.royaumedesidees.augustin_jeune.quete: You look different. Go and see Ambrose, before I change your mind.
You look like a pear thief. Come on, let's take %1$s: not because we're hungry, just for the pleasure of it.
The fig tree in the garden… I never go there. People cry too much there.
You, converted? Me too, one day. "Grant me chastity, but not yet."
%1$s more pear(s)! See Lucius's orchard? Nobody's watching.
Ha! We won't even eat them: we'll throw them to the pigs. Well… They say at the library a bishop reads without moving his lips. Go and see, I don't believe it.
So, that bishop who reads without speaking? Go to the library, and be quiet for once.
pnj.royaumedesidees.augustin_jeune.vol: *runs up laughing* Well done! %1$s more and I'll tell you a secret.
pnj.royaumedesidees.augustin_jeune.vol_e: *runs up laughing* Another one? You have good taste… in theft.
pnj.royaumedesidees.monique.apaisee: *Monica smiles, at peace.* My prayers are answered. I can go in peace.
pnj.royaumedesidees.monique.bonjour: *Monica weeps.* So many tears… The son of so many tears cannot perish.
pnj.royaumedesidees.monique.nourrie: *Monica eats in silence, then blesses you.*
pnj.royaumedesidees.monique.pas_mon_fils: It is not for you that I weep today. But I will pray for you too.
pnj.royaumedesidees.monique.priere: *Monica prays in silence.* As long as no one sins, I can pray in peace.
pnj.royaumedesidees.monique.repue: Thank you, but I have already eaten today. Keep it for the poor.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.bonjour: The heart has its reasons which reason does not know. My father's accounts, however, have none.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.attend: I am waiting for your sum, in the chat.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.debut: My father, Étienne, apportions the taxes of Normandy. He spends his nights on sums in livres, sols and deniers: 20 sols make a livre, 12 deniers make a sol. Help him. Answer in the chat like this: "19 livres 3 sols 0 deniers".
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.faux: Wrong. My father will spend another night on his accounts. Come back to me to try this sum again.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.fin: Perfect. But one would need a machine to do these sums… a machine that calculates by itself. I shall think about it.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.format: I did not understand. Give three numbers: livres, sols, deniers. Come back to me to try again.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.juste: Right. My father will sleep a little longer tonight. The next one:
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.somme: Sum %1$s of %2$s: %3$s, plus %4$s, plus %5$s. How much? You have %6$s seconds.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.impots.temps: Too slow. My father must have finished before dawn. Come back to me.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.pas_assez_de_: To change your Way, you would need %1$s Grace. Come back later.
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.raison: "Man is only a reed, the weakest in nature; but he is a thinking reed."
pnj.royaumedesidees.pascal.retour_raison: Back to Reason? The heart has its reasons… but accounts have theirs.
